hints: Focus on what happens when an ester is heated with aqueous NaOH, which part becomes the carboxylate and which part becomes the alcohol?
Ethyl propanoate, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOCH}_2\text{CH}_3$, hydrolyses to give ethanol, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$, as the alcohol product.
Now join that alcohol to 2-methylpropanoic acid, $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CHCOOH}$, by removing water to form the ester link $\text{-COO-}$ and check which structure matches.
walkthrough:
**Hydrolyse the first ester**

Think of alkaline hydrolysis as splitting the ester at the single C-O bond. The acyl side forms the sodium salt, the alkoxy side forms the alcohol.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOCH}_2\text{CH}_3 + \text{NaOH} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COO}^-\text{Na}^+ + \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$$

**Identify the alcohol clearly**

The name ethyl propanoate tells you the alcohol part is ethyl. So the product is ethanol, a simple 2-carbon primary alcohol.

$$\text{alcohol} = \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$$

**Identify the second acid**

Methylpropanoic acid is 2-methylpropanoic acid, a branched 4-carbon acid. Its skeleton is a central CH joined to two $\text{CH}_3$ groups and a $\text{COOH}$ group.

$$\text{acid} = \text{CH}_3\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)\text{COOH}$$

**Make the second ester**

Esterification joins acid + alcohol with loss of water. The acid provides the $\text{C=O}$ side, the alcohol provides the O-alkyl side.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)\text{COOH} + \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)\text{COOCH}_2\text{CH}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Match to the structure**

That product is ethyl 2-methylpropanoate: $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{-O-C(=O)-CH(CH}_3\text{)-CH}_3$. This is exactly the structure shown in the correct option.

options.A: Correct. It shows $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{O-C(=O)-CH(CH}_3\text{)CH}_3$, which is ethanol joined to 2-methylpropanoic acid. The left side is the 2-carbon ethoxy group from hydrolysis, the right side is the branched 2-methylpropanoyl group.
options.B: Incorrect. This is propyl 2-methylpropanoate, with a 3-carbon $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{O-}$ group. Students choose this if they think the alcohol from ethyl propanoate was propanol instead of ethanol.
options.C: Incorrect. This is 2-methylpropyl ethanoate, $\text{CH}_3\text{COOCH}_2\text{CH(CH}_3\text{)CH}_3$. It swaps the roles, using ethanoic acid and a branched alcohol. This comes from confusing which acid and which alcohol are used in step 2.
options.D: Incorrect. This is 2-methylpropyl propanoate, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOCH}_2\text{CH(CH}_3\text{)CH}_3$. It uses the original propanoate acid part and a branched alcohol. This is the trap of re-using the first ester acid instead of the new methylpropanoic acid.
